plain: The podcast host Jesse Michels often describes work by an astronomer named Beatriz Villarroel, who studied old photographic plates from the Palomar Observatory in California, taken from 1949 to 1957, before the first satellite, Sputnik, went up. Michels says she found many "transients," brief flashes that look like sunlight bouncing off flat, mirror-like objects in orbit, and he gives counts ranging from over 10,000 a year to over 100,000 in total, sometimes adding that they seem linked to nuclear tests. Villarroel herself, on the show, says 30 to 35 percent of the objects she studies come from solar reflections, which would mean something reflective was up there before humans put anything in space.
